item.title: Trump administration moves to impose more than $100,000 fee for H-1B worker visas
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration on Monday released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented fee of more than $100,000 on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers that has been blocked by the courts.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Wiessner
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump 's administration on Monday released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented fee of more than $100,000 on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers that has been blocked by the courts. The fee, first temporarily imposed by Trump last year, dramatically raises the cost of visas that are heavily relied on in the tech, education and research sectors. A federal judge in June [USN:L1N42G0QS TEXT:"ruled that the fee was illegal"] and blocked the Trump administration from collecting it. A Boston-based appeals court is [USN:O8N42O018 TEXT:"reviewing that decision"] while a different court considers whether a judge properly rejected a challenge to the fee by a major business group. Trump's temporary fee increase expires in September, one year after it was issued. The proposed rule by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, posted in the Federal Register on Monday, would make a fee of $103,265 permanent. It could be finalized by the end of the year. The H-1B program allows U.S. employers [USN:L6N3V704Y TEXT:"to hire foreign workers"] with training in specialty fields and offers 65,000 visas annually, with another 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees, approved for three to six years. Those visas typically came with fees between $2,000 and $5,000 before Trump's order. Trump's order did not apply to visas granted to foreign citizens already in the United States on student visas, who make up a large share of new H-1B recipients, or to renewals of current visas, but it appeared that the proposed rule would. DEBATE OVER VISA PROGRAM Trump, a Republican, and other critics of the H-1B program [USN:L3N3V90SB TEXT:"say it is abused"] by many companies who replace American workers with cheaper foreign labor. But business groups and many individual companies have said the visa program is needed to address a lack of qualified American workers for some jobs and to allow U.S. businesses to recruit top talent. About 70 employers had paid the $100,000 fee on a total of 85 visa applications as of late February, according to court filings. In imposing the fee, Trump invoked the president's power under immigration law to restrict the entry of certain foreign nationals who would be detrimental to U.S. interests. The fee is being challenged [USN:L2N3VX0TM TEXT:"by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce"], the largest U.S. business lobbying group, Democratic-led states and a coalition of unions and employers. Those lawsuits could be amended to challenge the rule proposed this week once it is finalized. LEGAL CHALLENGES MOUNT The lawsuits claim that Trump's power to restrict entry does not allow him to override the law that created the H-1B visa program. The states and groups that sued also say that the Homeland Security Department cannot impose fees, taxes or other means to generate revenue for the United States without permission from Congress. The Trump administration has maintained that the fee is not a traditional tax and that courts have little power to question the president's authority to restrict entry into the country. Amid Trump's broader immigration crackdown, employers last year registered for about 344,000 H-1B visas, down more than 25% from 2024 and fewer than half of the 759,000 visas sought in 2023, according to data from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. The Trump administration has also [USN:L8N3X92KM TEXT:"ordered enhanced vetting"] of H-1B applicants and proposed a new visa selection process that would favor higher-skilled and better-paid workers. Earlier in August, the Department of Homeland Security in a separate rule added fees of up to $4,500 to applications to extend the stay of H-1B workers or to transfer employees based in other countries to the United States.

item.title: Museum heists have turned more violent, with thieves hired on social media, Europol says
item.description: Art thieves in Europe are committing more violent robberies focusing on gold and jewels, and specialist gangs have been replaced by ad-hoc opportunists recruited through social media, Europol said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Julia Payne
item.content:encoded: Art thieves in Europe are committing more violent robberies focusing on gold and jewels, and specialist gangs have been replaced by ad-hoc opportunists recruited through social media, Europol said on Monday. The heist at the [USN:L2N3W000K TEXT:"Louvre Museum"] in Paris in October last year was a prime example of these shifts, Europol said, as the thieves threatened guards and visitors, and stole €88 million worth of jewels such as Empress Eugenie's [USN:L1N3W20UL TEXT:"tiara"]. Over the last two years, art thieves have shifted their attention to precious metals, jewels and cultural artefacts that offer greater profits, the EU's law enforcement agency said in a report. The price of gold has [USN:L8N44A0UZ TEXT:"surged"] 85% over the past two years, as investors and central banks turn to the metal as a safe haven. The London Bullion Market Association, which oversees London's over-the-counter gold trading hub, has warned that "as gold prices rise to historic levels, illicit flows and market distortions are also increasing." Europol said: "offenders are breaching premises and display cases using tools such as sledgehammers, axes, crowbars and, in some instances, explosives." Where traditional gangs used "deception and stealth", had a central leader and niche expertise, recent thefts were carried out by a decentralised ad-hoc group of profit-seeking opportunists, recruited through social media on a "crime-as-a-service" basis, it said. Europol added thieves were increasingly targeting gold items from nuggets and coins to jewels. "Precious metals can be easily melted down, leaving no trace for law enforcement, and facilitating illicit sales during the fencing process. Precious stones in jewellery, on the other hand, can be easily removed and sold further," the report said. In January last year, thieves used [USN:L1N40L0IB TEXT:"explosives"] to steal a 2,500-year-old Dacian golden helmet and three ancient gold bracelets from a museum in the Netherlands. The artefacts were later recovered and returned to Romania, although one bracelet is still missing. Europol also noted an increase in thefts of ancient Chinese porcelain artefacts such as Ming Dynasty vases due to high demand.

item.title: 米長期債買い戻し、財務省が手元資金活用を視野との報道－利回り低下
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ベッセント米財務長官は24日、長期債買い戻しの原資に財務省が手元資金の一部を充てる可能性があると報じられる中、債券に関して踏み込んだ発言を行うことを避けた。

イランへの経済措置を発表した記者会見で、買い戻しを近くさらに拡大するのかと問われ、「われわれはまだ債券を1つも購入していない」と述べた。

ベッセント氏は先週、長期債利回りが数年ぶりの高水準に跳ね上がったことを受けて、長期債買い戻しの増額計画を発表した。この日の会見で国債入札の発行額を減らすことも検討しているのかと聞かれ、財務省は「通常の発行計画を継続する」と説明。11月初めに予定される次回の四半期定例入札発表までは、変更しない考えを示した。

これに先立ち、CNBCは、金利上昇抑制を狙った長期債買い戻し拡大の原資として、財務省が手元資金の一部を取り崩す可能性があると、財務省高官2人の話として報じていた。

CNBCによると、財務省は連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）に預けている資金である財務省一般勘定（TGA）を利用する可能性がある。債券ディーラーは、財務省が1年以内に償還を迎える財務省短期証券（Tビル）など、より短期の国債を追加発行して買い戻し資金を調達するとみていた。

同勘定の8月20日時点の残高は9350億ドル（約148兆7300億円）。財務省はこれまで、予定される支出に備えるため、相当規模の残高を維持してきた。

財務省当局者は今年、余剰資金の活用方法を検討しており、その一部をレポ市場で運用する案も視野に入れている。ただ、一部の市場参加者からは、制度を新設する手間に見合う公算は小さいとの見方も出ている。

モルガン・スタンレーは、「余剰」資金の定義次第では、財務省が買い戻し拡大の原資として800億－2000億ドルを確保できるかもしれないと試算している。

モルガン・スタンレーの米金利ストラテジスト、マーティン・トビアス氏は「財務省が現金残高の運用方針を見直す可能性は十分にある」と述べた。

item.title: 米財務省、国債買い戻しの資金に一般勘定を利用する可能性－CNBC
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米財務省は、利回りが高い既発国債の買い戻し拡大に必要な資金を賄うため、手元資金の一部を取り崩す可能性がある。米CNBCが24日、財務省高官2人の話として報じた。

CNBCによると、財務省は連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）に預けている資金である財務省一般勘定（TGA）を利用する可能性がある。同勘定の8月20日時点の残高は9350億ドル（約148兆7300億円）。財務省はこれまで、予定される支出に備えるため、相当規模の残高を維持してきた。

長期国債利回りが数年来の高水準に達したことを受け、ベッセント財務長官は先週、国債買い戻しプログラムの拡大に踏み切った。債券ディーラーは、財務省が1年以内に償還を迎える財務省短期証券（Tビル）など、より短期の国債を追加発行して買い戻し資金を調達するとみていた。

CNBCの報道を受けて米国債は上げ幅を拡大し、10年債利回りは一時4ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）低下し4.69%となった。

原題：Treasury Could Use Its Cash Pile to Fund Buybacks, CNBC Says（抜粋）

item.title: 米国債上昇、ベッセント長官とウォーシュ議長発言に手掛かり探る
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 24日の米国債は上昇。今週は市場参加者にとって重要な週となる可能性がある。ベッセント米財務長官と米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）のウォーシュ議長の発言が、今後の利回りの方向を左右しそうだ。

米国債利回りは幅広い年限で低下。10年債利回りは3ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp=0.01%）低下の4.71%、30年債利回りも同程度低下し5.24%となった。先週は30年債利回りが一時20年ぶりの高水準付近となったほか、米財務省が国債買い戻しの拡大を明らかにし、荒い値動きが見られた。

最大の焦点は、ベッセント財務長官が次にどのような措置を講じるかだ。同長官は前週、長期債の買い戻しを増やす計画を示して市場を驚かせた。債券保有者は現在、巨額の米財政赤字に対するベッセント氏の対応策について、具体的な内容を求めている。

ウォーシュ議長の発言にも投資家の注目が集まっている。カンザスシティー連銀が主催するジャクソンホール経済政策シンポジウム（ジャクソンホール会合）で28日に基調講演を行う予定だ。インフレ率が目標を大幅に上回る中、長期金利の抑制を図りたいベッセント氏の介入を踏まえ、FRBがインフレ抑制にどう取り組むのか、説明を求められることになる。

BNYのシニア・マーケット・ストラテジスト、ジェフ・ユー氏は「市場は今週、ウォーシュ氏がFRB議長として初めて臨むジャクソンホールでの講演を見据えた展開となるだろう」と述べ、「長期債がなお不安定な状況にある中、投資家は財務省の措置にFRBがどう対応するのかを知りたがっている」と続けた。

26日に発表される7月の米個人消費支出（PCE）価格指数も重要になると、ユー氏は指摘。ブルームバーグが調査したエコノミストは、前年比の伸びが前月の3.7%から3.6%へと小幅に鈍化すると予想している。コア指数は3.3%で横ばいとなる見通しだ。

ウォーシュ氏自身は5月の就任以降、金利の先行きについてほとんど手掛かりを示していない。前回の連邦公開市場委員会（FOMC）金融政策会合後の同氏の発言が大規模な売りを誘ったこともあり、28日に予定される発言を巡って、市場は神経質になっている。

item.title: イラン産原油、中国向け供給は既にほぼ途絶－通貨リアルは過去最安値
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： イランのアジア向け原油出荷は、既にほぼ途絶えている。米国はイランとその貿易相手国を孤立させる新たな措置を近く発表する予定だが、発表を前にイラン産原油のアジア向け価格は数年ぶりの高水準となっている。

また、イランの通貨リアルの取引データを追跡するウェブサイト、ボンバストによると、24日の非公式市場でリアルは1ドル＝199万2000リアルと過去最安値を付けた。トランプ米大統領が先週、「いかなる国に対してもこれまで実施されたことのない、最も強力な経済作戦を発表する！」と表明して以降の下落率は4.5%に達した。

非公式取引のデータを収集するもう一つのウェブサイト、TGJUでは23日にリアルは一時1ドル＝200万リアルの節目を割り込んだ。ただ、終値ではやや持ち直した。

イランが輸出する原油の大半は、中国の民間製油会社が購入してきた。だが、ここ数週間はアジアで買い入れが可能なイラン産原油の供給がほぼなくなり、提示価格は世界の原油指標に対してディスカウントから、1バレル当たり4ドル前後のプレミアムへと転じたという。交渉に関与するトレーダーが、匿名を条件に明らかにした。

この供給途絶は、米国の海上封鎖が功を奏している部分が大きい。原油を積載したイランの船舶はペルシャ湾内に閉じ込められ、空荷の船舶は湾外で足止めされている。

調査会社ケプラーによると、その結果、中国などアジアの買い手にとって主要な洋上保管・積み替え拠点であるマレー半島東方の海域にある原油は現在わずか4000万バレルに過ぎず、そのうち売却先が決まっていない原油はわずか400万バレルと見積もられている。これは超大型原油タンカー（VLCC）2隻分でしかない。

ベッセント米財務長官は24日、イランを経済的に完全に孤立させる「前例のない規模の」計画を発表する予定だ。中国の石油精製業者や関連企業に資金を提供する銀行が標的となる公算大きい。だが、原油価格が高騰し供給が底を突いている現在、米国の計画に伴う財政的・外交的コストも一段と注目されそうだ。

item.title: 原油再急騰が米株最大のリスク、エネルギー株でヘッジを－モルガンS
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： モルガン・スタンレーのマイケル・ウィルソン氏は、原油価格の再急騰が米国株にとって最大のリスクだとの見方を示し、ポートフォリオのリスクを低減する手段として、エネルギー株を活用するよう推奨している。

ウィルソン氏によると、原油価格がさらに上昇すれば債券利回りを押し上げ、米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）のウォーシュ議長は、インフレ率を目標に戻すために対応を迫られる可能性がある。

ウィルソン氏は「対応の中心は財務省よりもFRBになるだろう。最終的にFRBが対応することにほとんど疑いはないが、その前に市場がさらに不安定になる可能性が高い」と述べた。

米イランの戦闘再燃や和平協議の遅れを背景に、北海ブレント原油は7月初旬から約30%上昇し、1バレル＝93ドル前後で取引されている。米30年債利回りは先週、約20年ぶりの高水準近くまで上昇し、米財務省は国債の買い戻しを拡大する方針を発表した。

ウィルソン氏によると、原油価格が上昇した際の株式への打撃は、下落の際の恩恵より大きく、原油相場の安定が株式市場にとって一段と重要になっている。同氏は、原油価格が急騰するリスクへのヘッジとして、エネルギー株を活用することを推奨した。エクソンモービル・ホールディングスとシェブロンの株価は今年30%超上昇し、S&P500種株価指数の上昇率の2倍超となっている。

また、利益が安定し、利益率が高く、効率的な事業運営を行う「クオリティー株」を選好する姿勢も改めて示した。S&P500はクオリティー企業の比重が高く、7月に半導体株主導で相場が下落した際にも、より大幅な下落を免れたという。S&P500は21日、過去最高値を2%弱下回る水準で取引を終えた。

S&P500などの指数の構成も、ウィルソン氏が米国株を海外株より選好する理由の一つだ。同氏は、半導体株が短期的に再び相場の主導役となる可能性は低いとの見通しを示した。

item.title: Exclusive-India plans first tokenised bond issue in September, sources say
item.description: India will launch tokenised corporate bonds next month, as it tests the use of blockchain technology to enable instant settlement of bond transactions, thre...
item.dc:creator: Khushi Malhotra
item.content:encoded:
Exclusive-India plans first tokenised bond issue in September, sources say

A man walks past an Indian Rupee symbol installation at the RBI headquarters in Mumbai · Reuters Khushi Malhotra Mon, August 24, 2026 at 6:24 AM EDT 2 min read

By Khushi Malhotra MUMBAI, Aug 24 (Reuters) - India will launch tokenised corporate bonds next month, as it tests the use of blockchain technology to enable instant settlement of bond transactions, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter said on Monday. The notes, to be issued for the first time by state-owned power financier REC, would place India alongside markets such as Europe and Hong Kong in using the technology for issuance and settlement.

Tokenised bonds are securities whose ownership, issuance, trading and settlement are recorded digitally on a blockchain or distributed ledger, allowing transactions to be completed almost instantly. India's markets regulator and central bank are working together on pushing the technology, according to the sources, who spoke on the condition of anonymity as the discussions are ongoing and confidential. REC will issue tokenised bonds worth less than 5 billion rupees ($57 million) in the offering, the sources said. The offering is expected to be unveiled at an annual financial technology event in Mumbai next month, one of the sources said. India's central bank digital currency will be used to buy the tokenised bonds, one of the sources said. Details about the issuer, timeline and framework have not been reported previously. "The offering would be made available to only a select group of investors at the pilot stage," one of the sources said.

Reuters could not ascertain the names of the investors. The central bank, markets regulator and REC did not respond to emails seeking comment. NEW BOND FRAMEWORK To tap the bonds, investors will need to access two digital accounts: a wholesale digital currency wallet provided by a bank, and a new electronic securities wallet, the sources said. Indian depositories are developing an e-wallet, a first of its kind, called DEMAT 2.0, which will record bond holdings on a distributed ledger technology chain. "Subsequent trades can take place only between participants that hold both compatible CBDC and securities wallets," one of the sources said. The bonds will have an initial three-month lock-in and exchanges are expected to develop a secondary market for the tokenised bonds by December, one of the sources said. The securities will not be traded on the conventional electronic book provider platform, the sources said. Depositories NSDL and CDSL did not immediately respond to Reuters queries. (Reporting by Khushi Malhotra, editing by Jayshree P Upadhyay and Mrigank Dhaniwala)

item.title: Gold price gets US bond policy boost
item.description: Gold hit a three-month high as the US Treasury expanded bond purchases, weakening the dollar amid rising debt concerns.
item.dc:creator: Northern Miner Staff
item.content:encoded:
Gold price gets US bond policy boost

Colin McClelland | August 21, 2026 | 8:01 am Markets   USA   Gold

The World Gold Council identifies how bullion benefits from economic policy. Credit: Adobe Stock Photo by monsitj.

Gold’s surge to about $4,600 per oz. this week may have further to run if US policymakers increasingly intervene to hold down long-term borrowing costs, according to the World Gold Council.

Bullion climbed to a three-month high Friday after the United States Treasury unexpectedly expanded purchases of longer-dated government bonds, weakening the US dollar and reinforcing investor concerns over Washington’s growing debt burden — which hit $40 trillion just this week after doubling in less than a decade.

The Treasury announced Aug. 19 that it would double buybacks of longer-dated Treasuries after yields climbed to their highest levels in years. The move immediately pushed bond yields and the dollar lower while sending spot gold up more than 3% to nearly $4,500 per oz., its biggest one-day gain since February. By Friday, bullion had climbed above $4,600, extending its rally to a third straight week.

Cambridge University economist Mohamed El-Erian said the Treasury’s action was “not yield-curve control (YCC) but it might be a step in that direction,” a view highlighted by the World Gold Council in a report on Friday examining what the policy shift could mean for bullion investors.

The council argues that the Treasury’s announcement reflects a deeper challenge confronting US financial markets. Persistent fiscal deficits require ever-larger bond issuance while a rapidly expanding stock of outstanding debt must also be refinanced. At the same time, some of the market’s traditional buyers are becoming less dependable. Foreign central banks are diversifying reserves, and investors abroad have alternatives offering attractive returns.

Hedge funds

Banks remain constrained by capital rules and corporate borrowing tied to artificial intelligence and data-centre construction is competing for investor capital, said Johan Palmberg, senior quantitative analyst at the World Gold Council . A growing share of Treasury demand now comes from more price-sensitive investors such as hedge funds.

Those pressures have left investors demanding higher compensation for holding long-dated government debt, Palmberg said. The recent rise in Treasury yields suggests markets no longer assume Washington’s expanding debt supply will be absorbed effortlessly, he said. Instead, the balance between supply and demand is becoming an increasingly important driver of bond prices.

If market pressures continue, policymakers could eventually consider yield-curve control, under which the US Federal Reserve would buy bonds to cap longer-term interest rates directly, he said. While the Treasury’s approach is being presented as a market-functioning measure, Palmberg suggested the distinction could become blurred.

“Just because it walks like a duck and quacks like a duck, doesn’t mean it’s a duck,” he wrote. “It’s monetary policy’s version of plausible deniability.”

Intraday reaction to Treasury buyback announcement on 19 August 2026. Source: Bloomberg, World Gold Council

The policy was used in the United States during the 1940s and has also been adopted in recent years by Japan and Australia. Unlike quantitative easing, which targets the quantity of bonds purchased and substantially expands a central bank’s balance sheet, yield-curve control targets a specific interest rate and can require much less intervention if markets believe policymakers will defend the ceiling.

How gold benefits

For gold investors, Palmberg sees three principal benefits if the United States eventually moves in that direction. First, yield-curve control would probably weaken the US dollar by shifting the adjustment away from bond markets and into the currency.

“The expensive US dollar is already facing pressure from several corners and YCC . . . could increasingly force the adjustment through the currency rather than the bond market,” he wrote.

Because gold is priced in US dollars, a weaker greenback generally makes bullion cheaper for buyers using other currencies and tends to support prices.

Second, capping government bond yields while inflation remains elevated would likely reduce real interest rates. Gold has historically performed well when inflation-adjusted bond yields decline because the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset falls.

Third, investors could increasingly view gold as protection against what economists call financial repression — governments holding borrowing costs below market levels to make debt more manageable.

AI issuance sourced from Dallas Fed  How AI debt financing impacts duration supply and interest rates – Dallasfed.org . Treasury issuance sourced from SIFMA Source: Bloomberg, Dallas Fed, SIFMA, World Gold Council

Uncertainty

“A Treasury market that clears at an administratively influenced price brings uncertainty because investors don’t know where yields would settle absent intervention,” Palmberg wrote. He added that “markets can be relentless. It doesn’t require aggressive short sellers . . . just an absence of buyers.”

Palmberg cautioned that the outcome would not necessarily be uniformly positive for bullion. A credible and temporary yield-curve control program could restore confidence in bond markets, compress risk premiums and reduce safe-haven demand for gold despite lower yields.

History also suggests such policies can be difficult to maintain. The US experience in the 1940s eventually collided with rising inflation and questions over Federal Reserve independence. Even so, Palmberg believes the broader investment case for gold remains intact.

“The debt mountain concern . . . remains one of the pillars of gold demand and any attempts to manage that burden not involving a reduction of debt or deficits are likely to continue favouring gold.”

item.title: China Considering Summit With Seoul in November, South Korean Foreign Ministry Says
item.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Wednesday that Beijing was “actively considering” a summit between the leaders of South Korea and China at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen in November, Seoul’s Foreign Ministry said. He made the comment at a meeting with South Korean Foreign …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Wednesday that Beijing was “actively considering” a summit between the leaders of South Korea and China at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen in November, Seoul’s Foreign Ministry said.

He made the comment at a meeting with South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun during a visit to Seoul, the ministry said in a statement.

Wang also invited Cho to visit China, and Cho accepted the invitation, the ministry said.

The ministers agreed to continue efforts to expand people-to-people exchanges, as the two countries forecast total travel between them to exceed 10 million visits, according to the ministry.

They also agreed to cooperate in various sectors, including negotiations on the service and investment sectors under the South Korea-China free trade agreement, supply chain stabilization, cultural exchange, and the adoption of Chinese pandas.

Cho urged China to play a constructive role in bringing North Korea back to dialogue as soon as possible, the ministry said.

Wang said China has been consistent in its policy regarding the Korean Peninsula, adding that he hoped for the peaceful coexistence of the two Koreas.

Separately, Chinese state media Xinhua reported that Wang called for “healthy, stable, and sustainable” ties between China and South Korea during the visit.

Wang said he hopes South Korea, based on its fundamental interests, pursues an independent foreign policy and develops relations with other countries in parallel without conflict, the report added.
